The points cover only NVIDIA; they contain no AMD or Intel material, so nothing can be said about what those two companies describe [0001045810-26-000021:0061].

NVIDIA says the possibility of additional export controls has hurt and may keep hurting demand for its products. It says this benefits competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted by further controls [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

NVIDIA warns that further export restrictions may provoke responses from foreign governments, including China, that hurt its supply chain or its ability to serve customers worldwide [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. China's antitrust regulators issued a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. controls, which required offering degraded products in China, violated the terms of China's Mellanox approval. Possible penalties and restrictions on its networking business could follow [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

NVIDIA says export controls have subjected downstream users to limits on use, resale, repair or transfer of its products, even outside China. They could raise costs or limit its ability to offer services such as NVIDIA AI cloud services, and could limit its CSPs' and customers' ability to serve their end customers [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

NVIDIA says controls have disrupted and could disrupt its supply chain and distribution channels, hurting its ability to serve demand outside China and for non-data center products. Reduced demand due to controls could cause excess inventory or related supply charges [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

NVIDIA also says deemed export control limitations could impair its R&D teams' ability to execute its roadmap on time. Repeated rule changes impose compliance burdens on it and its customers [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

For context on the direct effects, NVIDIA took a $4.5 billion charge in Q1 FY2026 for excess inventory and purchase obligations after the April 2025 H20 license requirement [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. Licenses granted in August 2025 yielded only about $60 million in H20 revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0061].
